source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"login", resource) when { resource.user == principal && context.credential.user == principal && context.enteredMid == principal.mid && context.passwordVerified };

name: inactive_session_blocks_assign_lhcp_to_hospital
rationale: The approved floor for assigning an LHCP to a hospital is scoped to an active session, and the specification states that after the inactivity limit is exceeded all authorization is disabled. Because assignment is a mutable administrative action, the active-session boundary needs a same-action safety property, not just a positive floor.
plain_english_summary: Administrators must not be allowed to assign an LHCP to a hospital when the request session is inactive.
source_excerpt: Electronic sessions must terminate after the configured inactivity period; after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled. The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.
reference_cedar: permit (principal is Administrator, action == Action::"assignLhcpToHospital", resource is Lhcp) when { !(!context.session.isActive) };
symbolic_verification_log: sugar-universal: ok (syntactic disjointness sanity check ok)

name: add_provider_only_own_list_active_session
rationale: The approved atoms do not yet include any safety bound for the addProviderToList workflow. Even though the search-by-provider-name requirement cannot be fully encoded with the current schema because Hcp does not expose a provider name attribute, the source still clearly scopes the mutation to the patient's own provider list and an active authorized session. This ceiling prevents policies from allowing a patient to add providers to another patient's provider list or to mutate provider lists without an active session, while leaving the unresolved search-name matching boundary visible for HITL/schema repair.
plain_english_summary: Patients should only be allowed to add a provider to their own provider list when the request has an active session.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"addProviderToList", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.patient == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: full_search_match_floor
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require the provider being added to match the searched provider name, specialty, and optional zip code.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: Not encoded: the schema has context.searchName but does not expose a name attribute on Hcp/Lhcp, so a faithful provider-name match cannot be written without a schema hook.

name: patient_can_add_provider_to_own_list_by_search
rationale: The spec explicitly grants patients the ability to add an HCP/LHCP to their provider list through a search workflow. This positive workflow is not yet covered by an approved floor, and the validated schema now exposes provider name, optional specialty, and optional zip-code hooks needed to represent the search boundary rather than using an arbitrary-provider proxy.
plain_english_summary: A patient with an active session should be allowed to add a provider to their own provider list when the provider matches the searched name and, if supplied, the searched specialty and zip code.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"addProviderToList", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.patient == principal && context.provider.name == context.searchName && (!(context has searchSpecialty) || (context has searchSpecialty && context.provider has specialty && context.provider.specialty == context.searchSpecialty)) && (!(context has searchZipCode) || (context has searchZipCode && context.provider has zipCode && context.provider.zipCode == context.searchZipCode)) };

alternatives_considered.label: own_list_only
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit adding any provider to the patient's own provider list with an active session, without checking the search fields.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"addProviderToList", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.patient == principal };

name: patient_can_add_provider_to_own_list_by_name_and_specialty_search
rationale: The spec explicitly grants patients the ability to add an HCP/LHCP to their provider list through a search workflow. The source says the patient searches by name and specialty, with only zip code optional, so this repaired floor requires a supplied specialty search value and a provider specialty match while keeping zip-code matching conditional on the optional zip-code search field.
plain_english_summary: A patient with an active session should be allowed to add a provider to their own provider list when the provider matches the searched name and searched specialty, and also matches the searched zip code if a zip code is supplied.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"addProviderToList", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.patient == principal && context.provider.name == context.searchName && context has searchSpecialty && context.provider has specialty && context.provider.specialty == context.searchSpecialty && (!(context has searchZipCode) || (context has searchZipCode && context.provider has zipCode && context.provider.zipCode == context.searchZipCode)) };

alternatives_considered.label: specialty_optional_when_absent
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit adding a provider when name matches and specialty is checked only if context.searchSpecialty is supplied. This was rejected because the source makes specialty part of the required search criteria and only says zip code is optional.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"addProviderToList", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.patient == principal && context.provider.name == context.searchName && (!(context has searchSpecialty) || (context has searchSpecialty && context.provider has specialty && context.provider.specialty == context.searchSpecialty)) && (!(context has searchZipCode) || (context has searchZipCode && context.provider has zipCode && context.provider.zipCode == context.searchZipCode)) };

name: add_provider_only_own_list_by_name_and_specialty_search
rationale: The approved add-provider floor is scoped to the patient's own provider list, active session, provider name match, required specialty match, and optional zip-code match. Because adding a provider is a mutable workflow and the source describes the search criteria as the boundary for adding a LHCP/HCP, a same-action ceiling is needed so a candidate policy cannot also permit adding arbitrary providers or adding to another patient's list.
plain_english_summary: Patients should only be allowed to add a provider to their own provider list when the request has an active session, the provider matches the searched name and specialty, and the provider matches the searched zip code if one is supplied.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"addProviderToList", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.patient == principal && context.provider.name == context.searchName && context has searchSpecialty && context.provider has specialty && context.provider.specialty == context.searchSpecialty && (!(context has searchZipCode) || (context has searchZipCode && context.provider has zipCode && context.provider.zipCode == context.searchZipCode)) };

name: personal_representative_can_view_represented_office_visit_information
rationale: The approved atoms include the patient floor and a ceiling for office-visit information, but they do not yet include the positive permission that a personal representative may view office-visit information for a patient they represent. This floor prevents synthesis from satisfying the ceiling with no representative access.
plain_english_summary: A personal representative with an active session should be allowed to view office-visit information in the medical record of a patient they represent when the record contains office-visit information.
source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see ... office visit information ... for ... records for whom the user is a personal representative.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewOfficeVisitInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && resource.hasOfficeVisitInformation && context has representedPatient && context.representedPatient == resource.patient && principal.representedPatients.contains(context.representedPatient) };
